name: Astra Orchestrator
tag: Hands work to subagents, then checks and improves the result before you see it.

scenarios.title: Write a product launch pack
scenarios.ask: Create a launch pack for our new scheduling app: {pieces} pieces of content, with {rounds} self-review rounds.
steps: Orchestrator
Split the job into {pieces} pieces: press note, landing copy, emails and social posts.
Writer subagents
Drafted all {pieces} pieces in parallel from one shared product brief.
Critic
Checked drafts against the brief. Found {=pieces + 2} issues, such as a feature named two different ways.
Reviser
Ran {rounds} review-and-fix rounds. Issues left: {=max(0, round((pieces + 2) / (1 + rounds * 2)))}.
Orchestrator
Packaged the final set with a change log.
followups: Why not always run three rounds?
Each round catches fewer new issues. Past two rounds you mostly pay for time with little change, so two is the default.
Can I see what the critic changed?
Yes. The change log shows each issue, the fix and which round made it.

scenarios.title: Answer a complex customer question
scenarios.ask: A customer asks for a combined quote across {products} products with volume discounts. Draft the answer.
steps: Orchestrator
Sent pricing to the Pricing subagent and terms to the Policy subagent.
Pricing subagent
Applied the volume tier for {units} units: {=min(20, round(units / 50))}% off.
Policy subagent
Checked delivery and payment terms for {products} products.
Self-check
Re-added the totals and caught one rounding error before sending.
followups: Does it send the quote itself?
Not by default. The draft goes to a person for approval. You can allow auto-send for quotes under a set amount.
What does the self-check look at?
Math, consistency with the price list and whether every question in the customer's message got an answer.

scenarios.title: Improve its own prompts
scenarios.ask: Our ticket summaries get {rating} out of 5 from agents. Let Astra tune its subagent prompts over {cycles} cycles.
steps: Collector
Gathered 200 rated summaries and the comments left by agents.
Critic
Found the main complaints: missing order numbers and too much background.
Prompt tuner
Wrote a new prompt version each cycle and tested it on held-out tickets.
Gatekeeper
Kept a new version only if it beat the last one. {=max(1, cycles - 1)} of {cycles} versions passed.
followups: A version only replaces the current one if it scores better on held-out tickets, and you approve the switch. The old version is kept for rollback.
No. It comes from test tickets. The real rating is measured after the new prompt runs live for a week.
